clips.end_words: accept the truth I give you
clips.caption:
A student came to a teacher demanding to be taught the secret of enlightenment. Instead of answering, the teacher started pouring him a cup of tea. The cup filled up — and the teacher kept pouring. Tea went everywhere, all over the floor.

"My cup is full, master. Why do you keep pouring?" "Because your mind is exactly like this cup. It's already full of what you think you know. Pour anything else in now, and it goes straight to the floor too."

You can't learn something new while you're still defending what you already believe. The emptying has to happen first.

clips.end_words: gurus always prostrate to someone else
clips.caption:
Every magnet has two poles. If you're standing upright, your head is the north pole and your feet are the south — and this isn't a metaphor, your body generates an actual magnetic field.

So when someone bows and puts their head near a teacher's feet, they're not performing submission. They're completing a circuit — pulling energy from someone carrying more of it than they are.

And the teachers who stay full instead of burning out are doing the same thing toward something bigger than themselves. The moment anyone says "I already know everything," they stop receiving, and start running on empty.

clips.end_words: how this was written and who wrote it
clips.caption:
In the Mahabharata, a blind king sits in his palace while a battle he can't see happens miles away. So he keeps a seer with him, someone who can remote view, and tells him: go watch the battlefield and report back everything.

A scribe sits there writing down what the seer reports, word for word, live. That's how this ancient text claims to have been recorded — not from memory years later, but in real time, from someone watching at a distance.

Believe every detail or not, the tradition is telling you something: this ability was assumed real enough to build a historical record on.
